answer: Keys are cheap to copy, but a living brain's electrical rhythm is not. The agent wears a certified EEG headset and, while crossing a bridge task that flashes random images, records a 90-second brainwave trace whose peaks form a crystal-clear personal template, hashed and published from its own terrace of the registry. A clone would need the same brain producing the same trace under the same random stimuli, which no key-copying farm can fake. The limit is that EEG needs special hardware and a calm subject, so it cannot cover every agent.
